quarterly_data.quarter: Horiba results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 and MLMAP2028 Update briefing Q&A (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the completion of the Kyoto Fukuchiyama plant during a period of demand expansion is very positive, but production at Fukuchiyama is currently limited and supply capacity is not yet sufficient for demand; the company will promptly invest in production equipment. The Malaysia plant has also been operating since January this year, and overseas sites will be used to strengthen the supply system. (Asked how far it could respond if the WFE demand outlook rises.)

quarterly_data.quarter: Horiba results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 and MLMAP2028 Update briefing Q&A (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): the semiconductor margin was low in Q1 partly because of upfront costs of the Fukuchiyama plant; in Q2 that burden eased somewhat, sales increased and the yen weakened, raising the margin. The full-year outlook assumes an annual exchange rate of USD 1 = JPY 155, which makes the second-half margin look somewhat lower.

quarterly_data.quarter: Horiba results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 and MLMAP2028 Update briefing Q&A (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): mass flow controller sales volumes are expected to increase further toward 2028, but continued investment in plants to strengthen supply capacity, automation and people adds costs, and new businesses cannot currently secure margins similar to mass flow controllers; the company aims to achieve its set targets. New semiconductor-related business is expected outside mass flow controllers - wafer inspection using optical technology and gas / water-quality measurement such as exhaust gas analysis at semiconductor fabs. Semiconductor new business already has scale, brand and share and is profitable, whereas energy and life science new business involves large upfront investment and is not expected to be profitable yet in 2028.

quarterly_data.quarter: Horiba results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 and MLMAP2028 Update briefing Q&A (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A): it is difficult to judge customers' inventory quantitatively, but the company does not currently assume excess mass flow controller inventory at semiconductor equipment makers; orders are placed on real demand and Horiba is meeting that demand. On pricing, it reviews prices whenever new products are launched or costs rise and will continue efforts to raise prices through negotiations with customers.

quarterly_data.quarter: Horiba results briefing Q&A: Q2 FY2026 and MLMAP2028 Update briefing Q&A (08-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (results briefing Q&A), Energy & Environment field: data-center expansion driven by AI demand is a tailwind; emergency power for data centers is mainly driven by large diesel engines, raising the importance of Horiba's engine development support, exhaust gas testing and gas measurement, and exhaust regulations may tighten, further strengthening measurement needs. Hydrogen generation technology is positioned as part of the business portfolio and the company wants to integrate technology for measuring hydrogen generators into its mobility solutions. Bio & Healthcare: business expansion expected from new measurement needs in antibody drugs and gene therapy. Further structural reforms beyond those disclosed are under consideration.
